items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like ground_px, main_pass and airborne_seqs are clear, but business logic uses single-letter names (m, p, c, a, f, w, h) and there are no docstrings. The airborne-classification rules carry only brief comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: analyze_video is about 170 lines and does everything: decoding, per-frame metrics, pass grouping and jump detection. It breaks the convention of a separate signal-to-takeoff/landing function. Peak-clearance and airborne_seqs append logic is copy-pasted, and per-frame values are printed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It checks cap.isOpened() and raises ValueError for short or no-pass videos. Magic constants are everywhere and unexplained (380, 25, 250, 340/375, GROUND_Y = 365.0, 550/350, 100..850, 30/20/45/50), and main() silently swaps a missing input for example_video.mp4.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: When no airborne sequence is found it writes made-up frames (best_frame ± 4) instead of exiting with an error. A missing input path silently falls back to /app/example_video.mp4. Every threshold is an absolute pixel value tuned to the example video.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: It reads argv[1] and writes /app/output.toml with exactly two int fields. But it falls back to example_video.mp4 when the path is missing, and the 0-based frame index convention is never stated.
